correctness.rationale: The proof normalizes every eight-point subset into one of 549 explicitly enumerated candidates in dimensions 3 to 7, derives an exact 8 minus twice Hamming-weight identity for every Fourier character, and exhausts every candidate with integer character summation and an independently implemented weight-four criterion. Exact tables agree; the nonzero restrictions lift with kernel fibers 2^(d-r), and all twelve normalized ambient values are distinct. Every sharp r=4 five-support normalized case is confirmed to have exactly one nontrivial period, yielding the unique quotient-simplex affine orbit. Full dimension-four enumeration of 12870 subsets independently corroborates the smallest strata. Finite computation does not purport to prove unrelated infinite claims; all ambient dimensions follow from a separate algebraic fiber argument.

value.rationale: Eight is the first size at which recent binary spectral-set work treats seven-coordinate evaluation codes and rank-dependent Fourier geometry. All twelve attainable exact Walsh-support counts are a natural, complete invariant; their disjoint scaled ranges identify affine span dimension using one Fourier statistic, and the sharp first nonaffine bound has a unique affine geometry. This is a complete natural classification, not an arbitrarily chosen numerical slice, and it resolves information not supplied by known weight-four criteria or one rank-six example.
